title: Shu Han
capsule: Shu Han (蜀漢) was founded in May 221 CE when Liu Bei, a Han imperial clansman, proclaimed himself emperor at Chengdu, claiming legitimate succession to the Han dynasty against the usurping Cao Wei and rivaling Eastern Wu. Its territory encompassed modern Sichuan, Chongqing, Yunnan, Guizhou, and the Hanzhong corridor — difficult terrain that constrained both expansion and invasion. Chancellor Zhuge Liang dominated policy under Liu Bei's son Liu Shan, launching five northern expeditions against Wei between 228 and 234 without achieving lasting territorial gains; his death at the siege of Wuzhang Plains in 234 left Shu without a comparably capable strategist. In 263, Wei generals Deng Ai and Zhong Hui executed a twin-pronged invasion; Deng Ai's audacious crossing of the Yinping ridge bypassed Shu's forward defenses, and Liu Shan surrendered Chengdu, ending the kingdom.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core territory in the Sichuan basin is well-documented in Sanguozhi and other Wei-Jin sources; exact boundaries of tributary zones in Yunnan and Guizhou are less precisely attested.
